27/10/2025 
 
UMI 
 
Attendees 
• Sarah Uzan – Director – UMI 
• Yaniv Nissim – Inventory manager - UMI 
• Hadewijch Tibos – Sales manager – ISZE 
• Jérôme Van Der Pluym – Assistant manager/pricing analyst – ISZE 
• Bart Symons – Strategic business developer – ISZE 
 
Wide Container Supply and Logistics Challenges 
• Ongoing issues with the availability of white containers for lubricant transport. 
• The problem is widespread, affected by traffic and import restrictions from 
Belgium, Turkey, Italy, but not the United States. 
• Shipments are being split into two containers, doubling shipping costs; this is 
due to the forwarder’s inability to provide the required containers. 
• ISZE & UMI are actively working to resolve the issue and will reassess in a few 
weeks via email. 
 
Competitive Parts Share and Sample Requests 
• Significant drop in competitive parts share: from 6–7% last year to 3,41% in the 
last three months. 
• Misunderstandings about sample requests clarified: the request was for BVP 
examples of items, not physical samples. 
• No change in procurement policy; preference remains for BVP and original parts, 
especially with Isuzu discounts. 
• ISZE will provide a detailed breakdown of competitive parts data by 
partner/group for review. 
 
Distributor KPI’s and Data Reporting 
• ISZE management requires monthly KPI’s from all distributors; UMI has not 
submitted recent reports. 
• Nadav is responsible for collecting and sending KPI data; some items cannot be 
provided due to system differences or internal policies. 
• Sarah will coordinate with Nadav to refresh the request and clarify which items 
can be shared. 
 
Business Planning and Market Information Requests 
• ISZE announced upcoming business plan preparation for the next year. 
• ISZE may reach out to UMI for market information to support planning. 
 
D Max Orders and Market Outlook 
• Over 1.000 D Max vehicles have been ordered and are awaiting delivery, with 
strong demand for the classic model. 
• The electric version is not expected to perform well in Israel due to range 
limitations. 
 
Follow-up Tasks 
• Continue working to resolve wide container supply issues (Sarah). 
• Wait a few weeks before proceeding with open lubricant orders and follow up via 
email (Jerome). 
• Refresh KPI reporting request and provide all possible data to Jerome, clarifying 
any limitations (Sarah). 
• Send a breakdown of competitive parts purchased to clarify the drop in share 
(Jerome). 
• Provide market information for business plan development when requested 
(Sarah).
docx: UMI
Attendees:
Shelly Cohen – Director - UMI
Yaniv Nissim – Inventory Manager -  UMI
Jérôme Van Der Pluym – Assistant manager/pricing analyst – ISZE
Bart Symons – Strategic business developer – ISZE
Sales Performance – FY2027 YTD
Sales reached €875K, 2% above budget but 14% below prior year.
Main negative impact was the suspension of the Shell lubricants business.
Growth was seen in nozzles, pad kits, exhausts, and body parts, while lighting and hydraulic/mechanical parts declined.
Shell supply remains challenging due to local price differences and limited packaging availability.
Genuine Parts Share & Market Coverage
Current genuine parts share: 54.2%; extended target is approximately 57%.
An incentive linked to the extended target is under consideration, pending approval from Japan.
Oil filters have relatively strong market penetration, while fuel and air filters remain lower.
Brake parts continue to underperform mainly due to price competitiveness versus alternative products.
Isuzu Dealer Standards Audit
Israel dealer average: 60.9%, compared with the network average of 74.8%.
Lower result was mainly caused by incomplete participation in Section E – Vehicle Sales.
Jerome presented a heat-map tool for identifying dealer strengths and improvement areas.
UMI will consider completing Section E so the results can be updated.
FY2027 Extended Target
Extended target includes a 1.8% stretch over the business plan, adjusted for declining fleet size.
Final locked target: €3,051,652.
Achieving the target will be challenging without Shell lubricants.
Alternative suppliers/products and special pricing opportunities will be investigated.
Special Price Agreements (SPA)
SPA was presented as an opportunity to increase parts turnover.
UMI to propose part numbers, estimated 12-month quantities, and target prices.
ISZE will review the proposal, negotiate where necessary, and seek management approval.
Previous SPA experience with UTI was cited as an example of the potential sales impact.
R&M Contracts / Fleet Tenders
UMI explained that fleet maintenance arrangements can include fixed discounts or per-kilometre pricing.
ISZE can potentially support major tenders through spot SPA/special pricing, subject to approval.
UMI will review the upcoming Electric Company of Israel tender and advise whether parts/R&M pricing support is required.
Sales-to-Dealer Data
ISZE requested monthly part-level sales-to-dealer data from 1 January 2025 onward.
Requested fields: part number, invoice date, and quantity; prices are not required.
Purpose is to improve demand visibility, replenishment, and sales analysis.
UMI will review the request internally.
Parts Training & EDI
New parts training includes a 30-minute online EQ Hits/order-system session and test for dealership staff.
EDI/order-type refresher sessions are planned for August and September.
ISZE will resend the invitation to Shelly.
Action Items
Jerome: Check availability and pricing of 5-litre Shell oil packaging.
Shelly: Send requested parts/oil list for price and availability checks.
Jerome: Review the list and investigate alternative suppliers/products.
Jerome: Communicate the genuine parts share incentive status once approved.
Jerome: Send the Dealer Standards overview and visualisation tool.
Shelly: Consider completing Section E of the Dealer Standards audit.
Shelly: Submit an SPA proposal with part numbers, 12-month quantities, and target prices.
Shelly: Review the Electric Company tender and advise whether ISZE support/special pricing is required.
